t.E1519.agn: In 2019 EFSA stated that its acute toxicity is low and that there is no concern for genotoxicity or carcinogenicity; on the basis of a rat carcinogenicity study it set the ADI at 4 mg/kg body weight/day. Estimated intake remained below this limit in all age groups.
t.E1519.body: Benzyl alcohol is converted to benzoic acid in the body; benzoic acid combines with glycine in the liver to form hippuric acid, which is rapidly excreted in urine.
t.E1519.found.0: Flavourings for liqueurs, aromatised wines and aromatised wine-based drinks (up to 100 mg/l in food)
t.E1519.found.1: Flavourings for confectionery, including chocolate, and some other products
t.E1519.prod: Produced chemically by reacting benzyl chloride, obtained by chlorinating toluene, with sodium or potassium carbonate.
t.E1519.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI 4 mg/kg body weight/day, no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E1519.summary: An alcohol found naturally in some fruits. It is used as a solvent and carrier in flavourings.
t.E1519.what: An alcohol used as a carrier solvent in flavourings.
